title: Cache warmup surcharge + micro‑tier doodles
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to capture an angle we haven't explored — explicitly charging (or crediting) for cold-cache/warmup cost and building a tiny micro-tier for edge interactions where warmup dominates unit economics.

High-level hypothesis:
- For very short, interactive sessions (<= 15s of generation / <1k tokens), the dominant cost is warmup (KV cache population + model weight mmap/transfer + first-token kernel overhead).
- A small surcharge or a pre-charged micro-credit can better reflect that cost and reduce downstream margin leakage on free/cheap tiers.
- Coupling this with a tiny micro-tier (low $/mo, tiny included credits, unlimited low-QPS burst allowance with higher per-token cost) can appeal to chatbot widgets, mobile microfeatures, and 3rd-party embeds.

Assumptions (back‑of‑envelope numbers — update with infra metrics):
- GPU reserved cost (amortized): $5.50 / GPU-hour effective (includes infra, ops, margin for RD).
- Avg live tokens/sec for short sessions: 40 tokens/sec during active generation.
- Typical short session length: 8s generation = ~320 tokens produced + ~80 prompt tokens = 400 tokens total.
- Cold-start penalty: 150ms extra latency + 0.6 GPU-sec of effective additional cost due to kernel startup + mmap overhead (measured on p3-like instance).
- KV warmup amortization: additional memory & compute ~0.4 GPU-sec per new session (small models less, big models more).

Convert to cost: 
- 1 GPU-hour = 3600 sec; 0.6 GPU-sec cost = (0.6 / 3600) * $5.50 = $0.0009167 ~ $0.00092 per cold session overhead.
- Per-token baseline running cost (steady-state) for short sessions: assume 0.0000009 GPU-sec per token -> per token cost (compute) = (0.0000009 / 3600) * $5.50 ~= $1.375e-9 * 5.5? Wait — simplify: pick per-token baseline infra cost = $0.0000025 (2.5e-6) per token. (We'll source actual metrics later.)
- For a 400-token session: baseline compute = 400 * $0.0000025 = $0.001. Add cold penalty = $0.00092 => total = $0.00192 cost per session.

Pricing levers / product patterns:
1) Warmup surcharge (per-session fixed): charge $0.002 per cold session (or consume 1 micro-credit). Rationale: keeps per-session pricing rounded, covers cold start and gives small margin.
2) Micro-credit pack: sell 1000 micro-credits for $1 (covering 1000 cold sessions). Effective cost to customer = $0.001 per cold session; margin depending on discount.
3) Micro-tier subscription: $4/mo includes 2000 micro-credits + reduced per-token price for steady tokens (e.g., 25% off). Useful for chat widgets with lots of short interactions.
4) Auto-warm discount: if a client pins a model or uses keepalive routing to dedicated warm pool, waive surcharge and charge a lower per-token rate (incentive to buy Dedicated or keepalive feature).

Break-even / margin check (rough):
- If we charge $0.002 per cold session and cost is $0.00092, margin per session ~ $0.00108 (~54%).
- If we sell 1000 micro-credits for $1 (avg $0.001 per session), margin per session ~ $0.00008 (~8.7%) — low unless this drives committed usage or reduces churn. So packs need to be priced higher (e.g., $1.50/1000) or tied to other upsell hooks.

Edge cases and UX:
- How to detect cold session? heuristics: no KV cache hits for user prefix, model not loaded on host for last N sec, or explicit header from client (recommended). False positives bad — avoid double billing on retries.
- Expose both: (a) surcharge that appears as line-item in invoices for transparency and (b) micro-credit auto-consumption for users on micro-tier/subscriptions.
- Allow customers to opt-out by pinning model or enabling keepalive (but premium price).

Interaction with existing constructs:
- Credits vs per-token: micro-credits are strictly for cold penalty; tokens are billed normally. Credits don't replace tokens. Avoid user confusion by naming: "warmup credits" or "session credits" (not "tokens").
- Competition: none of the major LLM API players surface warmup as a separate charge; could be a differentiator but also a friction point. Recommend framing as performance-credit: paying for faster cold-first-response SLA.

Variants to test (experiments):
A) Baseline: no surcharge, standard per-token pricing (control).
B) Surcharge only: $0.002 per cold session revealed on invoice.
C) Micro-tier: $4/mo + 2000 warmup credits + better per-token rate for short sessions.
D) Keepalive upsell: for high-volume customers, show projected $ savings if they pin model or enable warm pool.

KPIs to track during experiment:
- Cold-session ratio = cold_sessions / total_sessions (target: reduce via product).
- ARPU delta for micro-tier cohort vs matched control.
- Churn for users who hit many cold sessions (sign of poor onboarding UX).
- % of requests flagged as cold incorrectly (-> user complaints).
- Uptake on pin/keepalive feature and resulting cost delta.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get real numbers from infra: accurate cold-start GPU-sec, mmap costs, and token/sec for small/med/large models (ask infra/serving-runtime team). Linked PRIC ticket above.
- UX: mock invoice line, admin console visualization, and SDK header to opt-in/opt-out. (Add mock screenshots later.)
- Accounting: how to represent micro-credit liabilities on balance sheet (deferred revenue?). Talk to finance.
- Legal/regulatory: ensure no double-billing claims. Draft simple terms for micro-credits.

Notes / rough talk track for sales/marketing:
- "Performance-first micro-tier: avoid jitter and pay predictably for short interactive sessions. Micro-credits give you instant cold-response guarantees without committing to reserved capacity."
- For small SaaS widgets, savings from keepalive/pinning could be >40% on per-session cost once cold fraction is reduced.

Quick simulators (manual):
- If average user has 10 short sessions/day => 300/mo. Warmup cost at $0.002 = $0.60/mo. Micro-tier at $4/mo looks reasonable if per-token volume justifies the subscription (and they value better latency).

Final note: high variance across models (quantized LLaMA-7B vs FP16 Llama 70B). Need to categorize models into "warmup-light" vs "warmup-heavy" and apply different surcharge scales (e.g., 0.5x..2x).

Next steps:
- [ ] Ping infra for precise cold penalty numbers (PRIC-4123).
- [ ] Prototype invoice UI + SDK header flag.
- [ ] Draft micro-tier price ladder (1/mo, 4/mo, 20/mo) and run small user interviews with widget customers.

Random scribbles: half-life decay for micro-credits? Could auto-refund unused credits quarterly to reduce liability but that adds complexity. Might instead expire credits after 12 months.

End of scratchpad.
